name: Avarice-Shroud
geological_features: Stratified cloud layers rich in metallic compounds
Diamond precipitation in the deep atmosphere
Ammonia ice crystal formations in the upper bands
specific_features: A ring system composed primarily of gold-bearing asteroids
description: Avarice-Shroud is a gas giant that seems to mock the acquisitive instincts of every species that discovers it. Its atmosphere is stratified with metallic compounds that glitter in bands of copper and bronze, and deep-atmosphere probes have confirmed diamond precipitation at pressure depths that place the gems forever beyond practical retrieval. Its ring system, uniquely, is composed of gold-bearing asteroids.

The toxic atmosphere swirls with ammonia ice crystals that scatter light into auroral displays of breathtaking avarice, the planet wreathed in halos of gold and silver light as though wearing its wealth for all to see. The beauty is genuine and the promise is real, but the planet guards its treasures behind gravity, pressure, and chemistry that make extraction a ruinous proposition.

Microbial life thrives in the mid-atmosphere, organisms that have evolved to metabolize metallic compounds and whose biological processes concentrate rare elements in their cellular structures. Theoretical harvesting of these organisms could yield material wealth beyond calculation, but the organisms exist in atmospheric layers where pressure would crush any known collection vessel.

Avarice-Shroud has driven more expeditions to financial ruin than any other body in the sector, each one convinced it has solved the engineering challenges that defeated its predecessors. The planet's ring system alone has been the subject of fourteen failed mining ventures, its gold-bearing asteroids tumbling in orbits that shift unpredictably due to the giant's complex gravitational dynamics.
